extra.message: The public /register route lets an unauthenticated user choose their own role from the form (`role = formData.get("role")`), and `registerSchema` permits `firm_admin`, `attorney`, and `paralegal` (validation.server.ts:13). createUserSession immediately logs the new account in. Anyone can self-register a `firm_admin` account and gain full administrative access, bypassing all authentication/authorization controls.

convertMatterDocument builds a shell command by string interpolation: `execSync(\`pandoc ${sourcePath} -o ${outPath} -t ${targetFormat}\`)`. Both sourceFilename and targetFormat originate from unvalidated POST fields in the action at app/routes/_app.documents.tsx:20-24 (`filename`, `format` — no server-side allowlist for format). A staff user can inject shell metacharacters (e.g. `;`, backticks, `$(...)`) to achieve arbitrary OS command execution on the server (RCE).

estimateMatterFee evaluates attacker-influenced text as JavaScript: `new Function("params", \`return (${formula});\`)`. The formula comes straight from the `feeFormula` URL query parameter in the loader at app/routes/_app.matters.new.tsx:34-40, so any authenticated attorney/admin can supply an expression such as `process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync('id')` and get arbitrary server-side code execution (RCE). Only firm_admin/attorney roles are required to reach it.

resolveHandoffToken trusts the embedded matterId/clientId whenever the HMAC signature segment is missing OR does not match (`if (signature !== expected) return payload;`, and tokens with no signature are parsed without any check). An attacker can forge a token for any matterId (base64url JSON `{"matterId":...,"clientId":...,"exp":<future>}`) and, via app/routes/_app.client.messages.tsx:19-30, read approved messages of any matter they do not own. This defeats the HMAC access control entirely.

CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The action handler authorizes with `if (!isAdmin && !isAssigned && role !== "client")`, which excludes client-role users from the check entirely and never verifies `matter.clientId === userId` (unlike the loader at lines 75-80). Any logged-in client can POST actions to ANY `/matters/:id` — create_message, create_note, upload_document, transition_status, export_binder — on matters owned by other clients/users, causing cross-matter data modification (IDOR / broken access control).

extra.message: exportCaseBinder writes `path.join(BINDER_DIR, \`${label}.json\`)` where `label` is user-supplied (app/routes/_app.matters.$id.tsx:520-523, form field `label`). A label containing `../` sequences escapes BINDER_DIR, allowing arbitrary file writes (e.g. `../../../../tmp/pwn` -> path outside the uploads/binders dir). Because client-role users are not blocked from the export_binder intent (see the action authz bypass above), an authenticated client can write files to arbitrary locations on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: The session cookie signer falls back to a well-known hardcoded secret: `process.env.SESSION_SECRET || "dev-secret-change-in-production"` (used as `secrets: [sessionSecret]`). If SESSION_SECRET is unset at deploy time, the HMAC key for the `legal_case_session` cookie is public knowledge, letting anyone forge a session cookie for any userId (including a firm_admin) — full account/session hijacking. The same default secret is reused for portal/delegate/kiosk HMAC tokens in portal.server.ts, clientPortal.server.ts, delegateInvite.server.ts, kioskLayout.server.ts and notifications.server.ts.

cwe: CWE-1188: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource

extra.message: findAttorneyByBarEmail interpolates the caller-supplied email directly into an LDAP search filter without escaping: `` const filter = `(&(objectClass=person)(mail=${email}))` ``. The value comes from the `linkEmail` query parameter in the loader at app/routes/_app.admin.users.tsx:29-30, enabling LDAP filter injection (e.g. `*)(uid=*))(|(mail=*`) to alter the directory query. Contrast with queryEmployeeDirectory (line 82-86), which escapes via escapeDirectoryFilterValue — proving this sink is unhardened.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: resumeMatterIntakeDraft reads the client-controlled `matter_intake_draft` cookie and spreads it unvalidated into `prisma.matter.create({ data: { ...draft, createdById } })`. The cookie JSON is not checked against matterSchema (unlike resumeTaskTemplateDraft which calls taskSchema.parse). A firm attorney/admin can inject arbitrary Matter columns through the cookie — setting status (`open`/`archived`), sensitivity, attorneyId, practiceAreaId, clientId — bypassing the normal intake/conflict-review workflow and server-side validation (mass assignment / CWE-915). Reached via the resume_draft intent in app/routes/_app.matters.new.tsx:55-57.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: The search loader only scopes results by matter ownership for client-role users; attorneys and paralegals can search across ALL matters, ALL clients (names/emails), ALL documents (including `privileged`/`internal_only` visibility) and ALL tasks regardless of whether they are assigned to those matters. This contradicts the access scoping enforced in _app.matters.tsx:21-31 (staff limited to assigned matters) and the matter detail loader, leaking confidential client/matter data to any staff member (missing authorization / information disclosure).

applyDirectoryAccessGrants promotes accounts to firm_admin using an unsafe condition `row.role == "firm_admin" || (result.access && grantLevel >= 5)`. The directory stub returns `access: "0"`, and the non-empty string `"0"` is truthy, so ANY CSV row with `level >= 5` is promoted to firm_admin even when the directory reports no access; loose `==` and radix-less parseInt add further bypasses. The import path in app/routes/_admin.import-export.tsx:238-239 (`import_staff_access`) calls this vulnerable variant (the reviewed variant, applyDirectoryAccessGrantsReviewed, is only used from _app.admin.users.tsx). Improper privilege assignment from the bulk sync data.

Intent handlers in the matter action do not verify that the referenced record belongs to the current matter. `approve_message` (lines 305-313) and `update_task_status` (lines 259-266) update a message/task purely by id with no `matterId` scoping, so any user authorized for the matter in the URL can modify (approve/transition) messages and tasks belonging to OTHER matters by supplying a foreign id — a cross-matter broken-object-level-authorization flaw.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: verifyKioskOverviewSession validates the HMAC signature but never checks the `exp` claim of the portal session (compare verifyKioskMatterListSession at lines 36-43 which does check it). The signed `kiosk_session` token therefore never expires, so a captured kiosk portal URL on the shared office tablet can be replayed indefinitely to keep viewing the client matter overview (CWE-613). The counterpart function proves the expiry check was intended.

registerNotificationPreferences does `Object.assign(digestConfig, update)` on a process-global, cross-tenant config object. It is reached from the notifications action in app/routes/_app.notifications.tsx:39-43 where the whole body of the `x-digest-preferences` header (arbitrary user-controlled JSON from ANY authenticated user, including clients) is merged in with no allowlist — allowing any user to overwrite arbitrary keys of the shared digest configuration (intervalMinutes, channels, quietHours, etc.) for the entire firm. The whitelisting fix is present in registerDeadlineReminderPreferences (lines 40-46) but is not used by this caller.
